thread:
maya: Heads-up — our eu-west-2 firmware canary started showing a pattern: KVM proxy connections leak and the host flips secure-boot to enabled after a reboot. We've seen ~1.2% of canary nodes drop from the GPU pool. pausing rollout? :thinking:

sre-bot: ALERT: firmware-canary-eu-west-2 — 12 hosts evicted in last 10m, reason: 'secure-boot: toggled' (auto-detected). See /alerts/1746249999

raul: @maya can you paste the kubelet/jump-host logs for one affected host? curious if the KVM proxy error precedes the secure-boot toggle or vice versa.

maya: grabbing logs now. looks like kvm-proxy reports many CONN_RESET followed by a watchdog-triggered reboot. after reboot, BMC reports UEFI var changed. snippet:
```
[2026-03-20T10:02:11Z] kvm-proxy: conn-id=0x3f reset by peer, stream-killed
[2026-03-20T10:02:12Z] kernel: watchdog: hardware reset triggered
[2026-03-20T10:02:32Z] bmc: uefi: SecureBoot=Enabled -> SecureBoot=Disabled
[2026-03-20T10:02:33Z] provisioning: node rejoined; gpu pool status: 0 GPUs ready
```

elena: that's odd — var flip shows Enabled -> Disabled in the snippet. earlier slack threads showed the flip into Enabled. either way it's toggling unexpectedly. any recent changes to our signer or image?

ben: Not in the signing pipeline. We did land a micro-rewrite to the OOB kvm-proxy that touched the keepalive logic last night (eu-west-2 canary window). rolling back the kvm change to the previous commit might prove if this is causal.

maya: rolling pause on the rest of the canary started. @ops-runner can you hold the eu-west-2 batch and prevent scheduled rolling reboots?

ops-runner: paused rollout and disabled scheduled reboots for the batch id=fw-canary-eu2-20260320. Also increased logging level on kvm-proxy to TRACE for affected hosts.

raul: quick triage plan: 1) reproduce locally with the kvm-proxy change disabled, 2) collect BMC UEFI var write trace, 3) check if TPM/secureboot runtime asserts are being triggered by an unexpected ACPI event. is that reasonable?

maya: yup. I'll scope one of the evicted hosts into the lab and try a controlled reboot with packet capture on the management network.

elena: note for capacity/cost — since 1.2% of canary nodes moved out of the GPU pool, autoscaler already spun up a hot spare in us-central to meet demand. that added ~2.3 GPU-hours and bumped cost estimates for the day. we should include that in the postmortem.

ben: if we confirm kvm-proxy is the trigger, we should hotfix the keepalive and roll a restricted patch that doesn't touch BMC interaction until we verify. also add a canary rule: if secure-boot var changes post-reboot, auto-fence the host before joining GPU pool.

maya: temporary mitigations: (a) hold canary, (b) increase BMC audit retention for affected hosts, (c) add kube admission check to block nodes with secure-boot != desired against GPU pools. I'll PR the admission check now. :eyes:

raul: thanks. assign owners? maya -> triage & lab repro; ben -> kvm-proxy rollback plan; elena -> capacity/cost tracking + postmortem; ops-runner -> blocklist and extra logs.

ops-runner: assigned and noted in incident ticket #INC-1746249999. Will post updates here when we have repro or rollback. :thumbsup:

maya: update in ~30m after I attach serial logs and lab repro steps. For anyone watching — avoid manual reboots of canary hosts until we confirm safe path.

sre-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: rollout paused, ticket INC-1746249999 opened, severity: medium (service impact: GPU allocation jitter, cost bump).
